newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to record close on Telmex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to record close on Telmex.

text.p: Mexican stocks took their cue from market heavyweight Telmex to rally to a record close on Monday, traders said.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 2.80 percent, or 95.22 points, at 3,492.17.
Telmex L series shares, which weigh most heavily in calculating the IPC, ended up 0.98 centavos at 14.00 pesos.
For some traders, Monday was the "first real session of the year" after the holiday season. Trading volume was average at 72.9 million shares, but improved on many recent sessions.
"The year really did start on the bourse today. We feel that buyers responded to gains by Telmex and on Wall Street," said Daniel Romo, an equity at the Bancrecer bank.

Dealers noted that CS Boston upgraded Telmex stock to a buy from hold during the session, while Bear Stearns raised its 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates. Both brokerages said hikes in local call charges as of January 1 were a factor.
Telmex ADRs also climbed 2-1/2 to 35-7/8 in New York.
"It was high time dealers took a good look at Telmex. It was in heavy demand from foreign investors," a trader said.
Analysts noted that blue chips other than Telmex also gained on a combination of expected forthcoming falls in primary rates and technical factors.

"Some blue chips closed at resistance on Friday, which was a curtain-raiser for a session like we had today. Furthermore, after breaking through the 3,450-point barrier we were in an outright upward short-term channel line," a technical analyst said.
Analysts noted that after breaking the previous record close of 3,433.75 -- set August 27, 1996 -- the IPC was now in a fluctuation band ranging between 3,454 and 3,530 points.
"Nonetheless, we first need to validate the 3,500-point mark with a bit more volume," the analyst added.
Money market traders said they expected primary rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes to fall by up to 75 basis points at Tuesday's primary auction.
Blue chips that chalked up notable gains included media group Televisa and holding company Alfa, up 2.50 and 1.40 pesos, respectively, to 103.30 and 37.90 pesos.
The broad market scoreboard reflected the optimistic mood for blue chips. Out of a total of 103 stocks traded, gainers beat decliners by 71 to 20.
Pharmaceutical firm Autrey headed the gainers, up 1.40 pesos to 16.50 pesos. "Autrey had lagged behind the market and had to wait until today to get moving," a floor trader said.
Hotel operator Posadas headed the decliners, off 16 centavos at 3.40 pesos.
"Most falls were speculative or on profit-taking, nothing special. Most dealers were too optimistic to sell very much," a trader said.
